name: TX-25
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district lean of R+11
Incumbent Roger Williams running with $1.1M cash on hand
No Democratic polling, fundraising, or outside spending evidence
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~2%
model.rationale: The R+11 district lean, Williams' incumbency and large cash advantage, and no visible Democratic campaign infrastructure all point to a comfortable Republican hold, consistent with markets pricing a Democratic win near 2%. With no polls or ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the baseline margin.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or a polling surprise, would be the first sign this is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-25 is a heavily Republican district west of the Dallas-Fort Worth area, with a partisan lean of about eleven points toward the GOP. Incumbent Roger Williams is running for reelection and holds a clear financial edge, with roughly $1.4 million raised and $1.1 million on hand. Democrat Dione Sims has no reported fundraising, and no outside spending has been recorded on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give Williams about a 95% chance of winning. The forecast expects a Republican margin of roughly fifteen points, with Sims needing an unexpected shift in the political environment or a late infusion of resources to make this competitive.
